question: In India, ’National Science Day’ is celebrated on February 28 to mark the achievement of which scientist?
solution:
The correct answer is __**C. V. Raman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Science Day** is celebrated on **February 28** every year in India to commemorate the discovery of the **Raman Effect** by Sir **C. V. Raman** on this day in **1928**.
 
• Raman was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930** for his groundbreaking work on the scattering of light, which came to be known as the **Raman Effect**.
 
• The **Raman Effect** is a phenomenon in which light changes its wavelength when it passes through a transparent medium, leading to the discovery of molecular energy levels.
 
• The celebration of National Science Day is aimed at spreading awareness about the importance of **science, technology, and innovation** in daily life and encouraging the younger generation to pursue scientific careers.
 
• Every year, National Science Day is celebrated with a specific theme. For example, in **2023**, the theme was "**Global Science for Global Wellbeing**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **C. V. Raman:**

 
 
• Born on **November 7, 1888**, in Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• He completed his education at **Presidency College, Madras**, and was a brilliant student in physics.
 
• In **1928**, he discovered the **Raman Effect**, which became a cornerstone of modern physics and spectroscopy.
 
• He was the first Indian to win a **Nobel Prize in Physics**, establishing India's global reputation in scientific research.
 
• He was also awarded the **Bharat Ratna**, India’s highest civilian honor, in **1954**.
 
 
 
• **Raman Effect:**
 
 
• The Raman Effect explains the scattering of light when it traverses a material medium and undergoes a change in energy and wavelength.
 
• This discovery opened up new avenues for studying molecular structures and has applications in fields such as **chemistry, material science, and biology**.
 
• The **Raman Spectroscopy** technique is widely used in various industries, including pharmaceuticals and environmental science.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Scientists Mentioned in the Options:**
 
 
• **Homi J. Bhabha:** Known as the **Father of India’s Nuclear Program**; he was instrumental in establishing the **Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC)**.
 
• **Vikram Sarabhai:** Known as the **Father of the Indian Space Program**; he played a pivotal role in establishing **ISRO** (Indian Space Research Organisation).
 
• **A. P. J. Abdul Kalam:** Known as the **Missile Man of India** for his work on ballistic missile technology; he also served as the **11th President of India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Science Day:**

 
 
• Started in **1986** upon the recommendation of the National Council for Science and Technology Communication (NCSTC).
 
• It is an occasion to honor the contributions of Indian scientists and promote the importance of **scientific research**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Raman Effect:**
 
 
• Used in **chemical analysis** to determine the composition of substances.
 
• Applied in **forensic science** for crime scene investigations.
 
• Widely utilized in **astronomy** to study the composition of distant celestial bodies.
